content: 1. Do not store medications in the bathroom as the environment may expose them to moisture and light, which can degrade their effectiveness. 2. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into drains unless explicitly instructed to do so, as improper disposal can harm the environment. 3. Discard expired or unused medications properly, following local guidelines or pharmacy recommendations. 4. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the medication. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. 5. This document is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your health needs. 6. Common side effects of this medication may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, headache, dizziness, or unusual fatigue. 7. This medication may cause your skin and urine to appear orange-yellow, which is a harmless side effect. 8. Rarely, delayed-release tablets of sulfasalazine may appear whole or partially dissolved in your stool. 9. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. 10. Serious side effects, though rare, may include severe allergic reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson syndrome), blood disorders (e.g., agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia), liver damage, nerve or muscle problems, and infections. 11. If you experience severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, seek emergency medical attention immediately. 12. Before taking sulfasalazine, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, sulfa drugs, aspirin, NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen), mesalamine, or any other substances. 13. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 14. Sulfasalazine may cause dizziness. Avoid alcohol or marijuana (cannabis), as they can exacerbate this effect. 15. Do not drive, operate machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. 16. Limit alcoholic beverages while taking this medication. 17. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. 18. Sulfasalazine is chemically similar to aspirin and may temporarily affect male fertility. 19. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Caution is advised, especially near the expected delivery date, as similar drugs may harm a newborn. 20. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. 21. Sulfasalazine may lower folic acid levels, increasing the risk of spinal cord defects. Ensure you are taking adequate folic acid as directed by your doctor. 22. This medication passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Discuss risks and benefits with your doctor. 23. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. 24. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 25. Sulfasalazine is very similar to mesalamine and may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., urine normetanephrine levels, liver function tests), potentially causing false results. 26. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. 27. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for poison control. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. 28. Regular lab and medical tests (e.g., complete blood count, liver/kidney function) should be performed while taking this medication to monitor for side effects. 29. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. 30. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 31. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. 32. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal guidelines. 33. This information was last revised in August 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most up-to-date and complete information about this medication.
